title.narrative: Increasing habitat protection in the Jantho Pine Forest Nature Reserve, Aceh, Indonesia, by intensifying post-relearse monitoring of a newly reintroduced Sumatran orangutan population

description.narrative: The purpose of this project is to monitor reintroduced orangutans and their habitat use outside of the current release area, and broaden the habitat monitoring and protection within the Jantho Nature Reserve. The project will accomplish the following objectives and associated activities: (1) Build and manage at least 3 satellite camps, by (a) training additional staff in nest surveys, focal follows, and habitat and wildlife survey methods, (b) conducting preliminary surveys identifying camp locations, access, transect viability, and orangutan presence (e.g., nest surveys), and (c) building satellite camps and extending existing trail systems; (2) Monitor released orangutans, focusing on health, diet, ranging, habitat usage, and behavior/activity budgets, by (a) using grid-based search methods and the distributed satellite camp system, monitor orangutans throughout the greater Jantho site; (3) Together with BKSDA staff remote monitoring teams to conduct monthly patrols for illegal activities, by (a) facilitating training programs for remote monitoring teams on conducting field patrols and law enforcement, and (b) conducting remote field patrols and recording all human presence and illegal activities encountered in the protected Jantho Reserve; (4) Conduct quarterly aerial / drone surveys of Jantho region to assess damage and threats and locate illegal activities, by (a) utilizing unmanned aerial vehicles (UAV), survey and map Jantho for identification and targeting of threats to the habitat.
